 Stocks, peso end weaker on sluggish Q3 GDP growth
 by 
 Joann Villanueva
 Nov 9, 2026
 6:41 PM GMT+8
 CONCERNS. The weaker-than-expected output of the domestic economy in the third quarter of this year, at 2.1 percent, resulted in the negative close of the Philippine Stock Exchange index on Monday (Nov. 9, 2026). The Philippine peso also ended weaker against the U.S. dollar. (PNA file graphics)
 MANILA – Slower domestic output in the third quarter of 2026 resulted in the negative close of both the Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) and the Philippine peso on Monday.
The local bourse’s main index declined by 1.46 percent to 5,677.92 points, and the broader All Shares by 1.08 percent to 3,183.52 points. 
Only the Mining and Oil index gained during the day, up by 2.34 percent 
Property, meanwhile, led the decliners after it fell 2.07 percent. It was trailed by Holding Firms, 1.94 percent; Industrial, 1.74 percent; Services, 0.88 percent; and Financials, 0.84 percent. 
Volume reached 822.34 million shares amounting to PHP5.98 billion.
Losers led gainers at 100 to 74 while 69 shares were unchanged. 
Philstock Research, in a market report, attributed the weak sentiment in the local bourse during the day to the report on the 2.1 percent output, as measured by gross domestic product (GDP), of the domestic economy in the third quarter this year. 
Data released by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) during the day showed that the latest growth level is weaker than quarter-ago’s 2.4 percent and year-ago’s 4 percent, which authorities traced to lower household spending because of higher food and utilities prices.
“In line with this, worries over the local economy’s outlook following the latest GDP print, together with the high inflation trend and possibility of another BSP (Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas) rate hike also weighed on the market,” the market report said. 
Last Oct. 22, BSP’s policy-making Monetary Board (MB) hiked the central bank’ key rates by 50 basis points, higher than the 25 basis points hike expectations, to combat expectations for further acceleration in domestic inflation rates. 
Relatively, the local currency weakened against the U.S. dollar during the day, finishing the day at 63.31 from its 63.05 close Friday last week. 
It opened the day at 63.06, and traded between 63.33 and 63.02. Average for the day stood at 63.25. 
Volume reached USD1.26 billion, higher than the previous session’s nearly USD1.2 billion. (Joann Santiago-Villanueva/PNA)
